propositions.text: Applicant seeks judicial review of Officer's refusal of permanent residence on H and C grounds under subsection 25(1) of the Act
propositions.quote: Mr. Shunli Liu (the “Applicant”) seeks judicial review of the decision of an Officer, refusing his application for permanent residence on Humanitarian and Compassionate (“H and C”) grounds pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, S. C. 2001, c. 27 (the “Act”).

paragraphs.summary: Applicant seeks judicial review of Officer's refusal of permanent residence on H and C grounds under subsection 25(1) of the Act, court states.

propositions.text: Applicant is Chinese citizen who came to Canada in 2008 and claimed protection as a practicing Catholic; RPD denied claim on credibility grounds in 2011
propositions.quote: The Applicant is a citizen of China. He came to Canada in 2008 and claimed protection on the basis of fear of persecution resulting from his status as a practicing Catholic in China. His claim was denied on January 5, 2011 by the Immigration and Refugee Board, Refugee Protection Division (the “RPD”) on credibility concerns.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant is Chinese citizen who claimed protection as Catholic; RPD denied claim on credibility grounds in 2011, court states.

propositions.text: Applicant submitted H and C request on September 18, 2018; denial decision dated June 17, 2020
propositions.quote: The Applicant submitted his H and C request on September 18, 2018. The decisions, denying his request, was dated June 17, 2020.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submitted H and C request in 2018; denial decision dated 2020, court states.

propositions.text: Officer found Applicant failed to address RPD credibility concerns
propositions.quote: The Officer determined, among other things, that the Applicant had failed to address the credibility concerns of the RPD.

propositions.text: Officer found Applicant failed to submit sufficient evidence that he could not practice Catholicism underground or that he fit profile attracting government attention
propositions.quote: The Officer also found that the Applicant had failed to submit sufficient evidence to show that he would not be able to continue practicing the Catholic religion as a member of an underground Catholic church and further, that he did not fit the profile of a “parishioner” who might attract the attention of the Chinese government and could practice his religion upon his return to China.

paragraphs.summary: Officer found Applicant failed to address RPD credibility concerns and failed to show risk to underground Catholic practice or government attention, earlier decision-maker found.

propositions.text: Applicant challenges Officer’s assessment of risk and adverse country conditions
propositions.quote: In this application for judicial review, the Applicant challenges the Officer’s assessment of risk and adverse country conditions.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant challenges Officer’s assessment of risk and adverse country conditions, applicant argues.

propositions.text: Officer’s decision is reviewable on reasonableness standard per Vavilov (2019)
propositions.quote: The decision of the Officer is reviewable on the standard of reasonableness, pursuant to the decision in Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v. Vavilov (2019), 441 D.L.R. (4th) 1 (S.C.C.).

paragraphs.summary: Officer’s decision is reviewable on reasonableness standard per Vavilov (2019), court states.

propositions.text: Reasonableness requires decision to show justification, transparency, intelligibility, and be justified by relevant facts and law per Vavilov para 99
propositions.quote: In considering reasonableness, the Court is to ask if the decision under review “bears the hallmarks of reasonableness – justification, transparency and intelligibility – and whether it is justified in relation to the relevant factual and legal constraints that bear on that decision”; see Vavilov, supra at paragraph 99.

paragraphs.summary: Reasonableness requires decision to show justification, transparency, intelligibility, and be justified by relevant facts and law per Vavilov para 99, court states.

propositions.text: After reviewing record and submissions, court finds decision does not meet legal test
propositions.quote: Upon considering the contents of the Certified Tribunal Record and the affidavit of the Applicant sworn on November 1, 2020, as well as the written and oral submissions of the Applicant and of the Minister of Citizenship and Immigration (the “Respondent”), I hold the view that the decision does not meet the required legal test.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds decision does not meet legal test after reviewing record and submissions, court finds.

propositions.text: Officer relied on 2017 report showing religious tolerance but ignored contradictory 2019 report showing risk to Catholics
propositions.quote: The Officer referred to a report that was published in 2017 to support the view that practicing Catholics are not harassed by authorities and that there is a “high degree of religious tolerance” for Catholicism in the Applicant’s home province in China. However, the Officer failed to mention more recent information contained in a report from 2019 that gave a contradictory view of the 2017 material. The Officer did not acknowledge the more recent material that addressed evidence of risk to Catholics and other religious minorities in China.

paragraphs.summary: Officer relied on 2017 report showing religious tolerance but ignored contradictory 2019 report showing risk to Catholics, court finds.

propositions.text: Failure to consider recent report makes Officer’s decision unreasonable, similar error criticized in Cepeda-Gutierrez
propositions.quote: In my opinion, this failure makes the Officer’s decision unreasonable. It is the kind of error that attracted criticism in the decision of Cepeda-Gutierrez v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship & Immigration) (1998), 157 F.T.R. 35.

paragraphs.summary: Failure to consider recent report makes Officer’s decision unreasonable, similar error criticized in Cepeda-Gutierrez, court finds.

propositions.text: Error is dispositive; no need to address other Applicant arguments
propositions.quote: This error is dispositive and it is not necessary for me to address the other arguments raised by the Applicant.

paragraphs.summary: Error is dispositive; court declines to address other Applicant arguments, court concludes.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review allowed, Officer’s decision set aside, matter remitted to different officer for redetermination, no question certified
propositions.quote: In the result, the application for judicial review will be allowed, the decision will be set aside and the matter remitted to a different office for redetermination, no question is proposed for certification. JUDGMENT in IMM-2870-20 THIS COURT’S JUDGMENT is that the application for judicial review is allowed, the decision of the Officer is set aside and the matter remitted to a different officer for redetermination. There is no question proposed.

paragraphs.summary: Application for judicial review allowed; decision set aside; matter remitted to different officer; no question certified, court orders.
